hook: My employer **hasn't paid my salary.** What can I do?

slides.title: Wages have a **legal deadline.**
list: Daily: at the **end of the shift.**
Weekly: last working day before the weekly holiday.
Fortnightly: before the end of the 2nd day after the fortnight.
Monthly: before the **7th day** of the next month ends.

slides.title: Left the job? **Two working days.**
slides.body: If you are removed, dismissed, retrenched or you resign, your wages must be paid within **two working days.**

slides.title: Deductions have **limits.**
slides.body: Your employer can deduct only what the Code allows, like fines, absence, advances or tax. All deductions together cannot cross **50% of your wages.**

slides.title: File a **claim** with the authority.
list: One application can cover several co-workers
slides.note: Which office? Depends on Centre or State.

slides.title: Time limit: **three years.**
slides.body: Apply within three years from the date the claim arose. Late? The authority may still hear it if you show **sufficient cause** for the delay.

slides.title: What the authority **can do.**
list: Add compensation up to 10 times the claim
Still unpaid? Recovery as land revenue arrears
Appeal lies within 90 days of the order

sources: Code on Wages, 2019 – Sections 2(k), 17, 18, 45, 49, 69 (in force from 21 Nov 2025, PIB)
Code on Wages (Central) Rules, 2026 – G.S.R. 343(E), 8 May 2026 (labour.gov.in)
Ministry of Labour & Employment – FAQs on Labour Codes & Central Rules, as on 25.10.2026 (labour.gov.in)
caption:
Salary not paid on time? Here's what the law says and what you can do. 👇

1️⃣ Monthly wages must be paid before the 7th day of the next month ends
2️⃣ Removed, dismissed, retrenched or resigned? Wages are due within two working days
3️⃣ Total deductions cannot cross 50% of your wages
4️⃣ You, your registered union or the Inspector-cum-Facilitator can file a claim before the authority under the Code; which office handles it depends on whether the Centre or your State is the appropriate Government
5️⃣ File within three years; a late claim may be heard for sufficient cause
6️⃣ The authority can order compensation up to 10 times the claim
⚠️ The Code on Wages, 2019 is in force from 21 Nov 2025 and replaced the Payment of Wages Act, 1936

Source: Code on Wages, 2019 (Sec 17, 18, 45, 49, 69)
